items.title: *** EDPS Press Release ***
items.description: *** EDPS Press Release *** In a new Opinion, the EDPS supports the European Commission’s proposal for the EU KIDS Act (EU Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy): protecting children online and preventing regulatory fragmentation in the EU. The EDPS calls for safety by design for all users. The proposal would introduce age limits, requirements on safety by design and age assurance for online services accessible to minors, such as social networks, video-sharing platforms, online games and AI chatbots. The European Parliament and the Council should carefully consider which features require age assurance, and where safety by design for all users would also be effective. The Opinion's recommendations include: ✅ age assurance and parental verification obligations should only enter into application when privacy-preserving solutions are effectively available across the EU; ✅ algorithmic age estimation and other intrusive practices should be expressly excluded; ✅ the GDPR should be amended so that a single age of consent applies to all information society services in the EU. items.title: 📣 TechSonar 2026-2027
items.description: 📣 TechSonar 2026-2027 The new edition of TechSonar is out now! This year, we look at emerging technologies and technology-related developments expected to gain relevance within the next three to four years, and at their potential impact on the privacy and other fundamental rights of individuals. This year’s 6 trends: ☑️ Internet of Bodies ☑️ AI integration protocols ☑️ AI-based employee monitoring ☑️ Digital content provenance and authenticity ☑️ Online age assurance technologies ☑️ Post-quantum cryptography Looking across them, the report identifies three common threads: the expanding role of technology in collecting and extracting data, the growing societal demand to establish authenticity, and an AI-versus-AI dynamic, with AI used not only to generate content but also to detect, verify and challenge it. Do you want to know more? Read the full report: ▶️ HTML https:// link.europa.eu/YvdKRj ▶️ PDF https:// link.europa.eu/dqw4Nt

items.title: *** Redefining the status of the DPO in Europe ***
items.description: *** Redefining the status of the DPO in Europe *** AI does not stand still, and neither can the role of the Data Protection Officer. @ Secretary_General Leonardo Cervera-Navas, delivered a keynote speech at the 28th International Information Security Conference ISMS Forum on the status of the DPO in the current AI ecosystem. He explained that data protection rules were built for processing operations that stayed still long enough to be described, whereas AI systems are constantly updated, infer new information and increasingly act on their own. He explained that this reality is redefining the DPO’s role, and called for that redefinition to strengthen the function rather than hollow it out. He set out how DPOs can stay influential throughout an AI system’s lifecycle: by being involved from the planning phase, by accompanying systems as they change, and by being able to say “not yet”. He also underlined that the AI Act correspondent role cannot replace the DPO, and that resources and training must keep pace with expectations. “In the new AI ecosystem, a DPO’s worth should not be measured by how many assessments they have written.
